'''''Luzula nivea''''', commonly known as '''snow-white wood-rush''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''snowy wood-rush''' and '''lesser wood-rush''', is a species of [[perennial plant]] in [[Juncaceae]] family.

The plant is native to Southwestern and [[Central Europe]], including the [[Alps]] and [[Pyrenees]].<ref name=monocot>{{cite web|url=http://juncaceae.e-monocot.org/taxonomy/term/1902|title=''Luzula nivea''|publisher=E-Monocot|accessdate=2 February 2014}}</ref>

==Description==
''Luzula nivea'' is {{convert|45|-|85|cm}} in length. Its basal leaves are {{convert|20|-|30|cm}} long and {{convert|3|–|4|mm}} wide.<ref name=monocot/>

Its lower bract is {{convert|10|–|12|cm}} long. Its anthers are {{convert|1.8|–|2.2|mm}} long and are brownish coloured, while its [[Stamen|filament]]s are {{convert|1.5|–|1.9|mm}} long with a {{convert|2.2|–|2.6|mm}} style. The species [[stigma (botany)|stigmas]] are {{convert|1.0|–|1.3|mm}} long.<ref name=monocot/>

==Cultivation==
''Luzula nivea'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental grass]], for planting in gardens.<ref name=monocot/> In some climates it can escape from gardens to become an [[invasive species]].<ref name=monocot/>
